variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Coordinates are [y, x]. The right-side target is the one with the SMALLER x; the left-side target is the one with the LARGER x. First read the goal to get the required number of target visits REQ: if it says 'repeating this back and forth motion N times' then REQ = 2*N (two=4, three=6); if it instead says 'then put it down on the left-side target' then REQ = 2. Every episode starts with subgoal A. Before applying the rules, compute this step's UPDATED visits_done exactly as the memory instruction says (carried-in value, plus 1 if the current scene shows the cube held AND a highlighted target). Every comparison with REQ below refers to that updated value, never to the carried-in value. Rules (apply whichever matches the current step and the updated memory): 1. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and visits_done is 0 (cube resting on the table, fingers open, nothing done yet): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the cube's center coordinates. 2. If the cube IS held in the gripper and updated visits_done < REQ: choose B, move to the top of the target, pointing at the target that is NOT highlighted in the current scene, using that target's listed coordinates. If neither target is highlighted (right after the pick-up), point at the right-side target, the one with the smaller x. 3. If the cube IS held in the gripper and updated visits_done >= REQ (the cube is now above the left-side target after the last required visit): choose C, put the cube on the table. 4. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and updated visits_done >= REQ (cube resting on the table after the put-down, fingers fully open, gripper raised): choose D, press the button. If no rule matches: when the cube is held, choose B pointing at the target that is not highlighted; when the cube is on the table and visits_done is 0, choose A at the cube; when the cube is on the table and visits_done > 0, choose D.

fields.name: visits_done
fields.description: Carry in the previous value (start at 0 on the first step, where memory is empty). Add 1 if and only if the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) shows the cube 'held in the gripper' AND a 'highlighted target' is listed in that scene. Do NOT consult the earlier execution frames of this step; it does not matter whether they already showed the highlight. Otherwise keep the carried-in value unchanged: if no highlighted target is listed (pick-up just ended), or the cube is not held (put-down ended with fingers fully open and the cube resting on the table, or the press-button step), the value does not change. Write the updated value; it is the value the subgoal rules read at this step. e.g. 3
fields.annotation: Number of completed 'move to the top of the target' subgoals so far in the episode, counting each arrival of the held cube over a target (right or left). It is 0 at the first step and stays 0 through the step that ends the pick-up. It increases by exactly 1 at each decision step that ends a B subgoal, i.e. every step whose final scene shows the cube held in the gripper AND a highlighted target in the scene. Whether the earlier execution frames of that step already showed the highlight does not matter: a step whose first execution frame already carries the highlight (a quick arrival) still counts as exactly one arrival. It does not change at the step that ends the put-down (cube no longer held) or at the press-button step. e.g. 3

history.critique:
field visits_done, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Number of target arrivals completed so far with the cube held. It is 0 at the first step and through the step that ends the pick-up. It increases by exactly 1 at every decision step whose final scene shows the cube held in the gripper AND a highlighted target in the scene (every step that ends a 'move to the top of the target' subgoal). It does not depend on what the earlier execution frames of that step showed: a step whose first execution frame already shows the highlight (because the arrival was quick) still counts as one arrival. It does not change at the step that ends the put-down (cube on the table, fingers fully open) or at the press-button step. Reason for the change: the old rule keyed the increment on the highlight being absent in the first execution frame of the step, but when the robot arrives within a frame or two, every shown frame already carries the highlight, so the policy kept the old count and the subgoal was then chosen from the wrong parity (PREDICTABILITY). e.g. 3

field visits_done, POLICY PROMPT
  Carry in the previous value (start at 0 on the first step, where memory is empty). Add 1 if and only if the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) shows the cube 'held in the gripper' AND a 'highlighted target' is listed in that scene. Do NOT look at the earlier execution frames of this step; it does not matter whether they already showed the highlight. If the cube is not held in the scene (put-down ended, fingers fully open, cube resting on the table) or no highlighted target is listed (pick-up just ended), keep the carried-in value unchanged. Write the updated value; it is the value the subgoal rules read. e.g. 3

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The failure: with the cube held and the right-side target just reached (highlight already present in every frame of the short step), the policy carried in 0, did not increment, and rule 2 then gave it two contradictory answers: the carried-in parity (0, even) said point at the right-side target, while the clause 'point at the target that is NOT currently highlighted' said the left-side one. It chose the already-highlighted right-side target; the recorded subgoal was the left-side target. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure caused by rule 2 reading the carried-in count instead of the count written at this step. Replace rules 2 and 3 as follows. First compute this step's updated visits_done (the memory you write at this step, per the memory instruction). Rule 2: if the cube is held and updated visits_done < REQ, choose B and point at the target that is NOT highlighted in the current scene (its listed coordinates); when neither target is highlighted (right after the pick-up), point at the right-side target, the one with the smaller x. Drop the parity clause entirely; the non-highlighted target is the whole rule. Rule 3: if the cube is held and updated visits_done >= REQ, choose C. Rule 4 unchanged but also read the updated value: cube not held, fingers fully open, gripper raised, visits_done >= REQ, choose D. Rule 1 unchanged. In the fallback sentence, keep 'when the cube is held, choose B at the target that is not highlighted', and state once that every comparison with REQ and every parity in this document refers to the updated visits_done written at this step, never to the carried-in value.
